topic: Cans came 40+ years before can openers

claims.claim: Peter Durand received a British patent in 1810 for preserving food in tin(-plated) containers - the tin can.
claims.note: One source says 1811; 1810 is far better supported.

claims.claim: The first can-opener patents came in the 1850s (UK: F. G. Yates 1852 / R. Yates 1855; US: Ezra Warner 1858) - at least 40 years after 1810.
claims.note: Exact first patent is disputed, so the script says '40 years' (true for every candidate date).

claims.claim: Early cans were thick and heavy (wrought iron lined with tin); some weighed more than the food inside.
People opened early cans with a hammer and chisel.
By the 1850s cans were made thinner (thin steel sheet).
claims.note: Sources differ on exact timing. Script states it alongside the openers appearing; it does NOT claim thinner cans caused the invention.

rejected.claim: Thinner cans are why the can opener was invented.
